name: Code health report
ownerWords:
i don't want to do per PR checks, but daily Git reports and keep track of metrics.
things are meant to be first written in plan -> achieved ->  cleared & written on duty for maintanence only -> and valiantly persued whenever not met. JUST DO IT
goal: The daily code health report keeps working: every day the report page on the wiki shows that day's numbers for auto-sns-agent and sieun-pi, the DuckDB store holds a row set for both repos for each of the last 7 days, the store box holds a fresh dated copy, and the daily run has no failed step. The run is code-health.timer at 06:00 KST on us-metal02 (auto-sns-agent scripts/dev/code-health-daily.mjs). These four metrics hold the problems that came back in this chat: missed report days (10-16, 10-17 and after the host move on 10-18), a failed store box copy (twice on 10-17), and test and CI loads that broke on GitHub's artifact quota (10-17 and 10-18, then the CI log reader on 10-18). The load-tests skip until 2026-11-01 no longer makes sense, because tests and CI now come from the CI job logs, so plan step p14 removes it from the precheck. When goal p12 is met for 7 days, its test and CI day count replaces report_days_7d as the headline. Goal p15 is met, so ranked_metrics_shown checks that the page shows all 8 ranked metrics with the newest day's numbers for both repos, and goal p12 (owner, 2026-10-15: "now the same system will monitor and report test stats, CI stats.") folds in as two more: auto-sns-agent's tests, counted only when that day's test load holds every suite the CI plan expects (auto-sns-agent scripts/ci/junit-suites.mjs, one junit suite per test task of scripts/ci/plan.mjs JOBS), and its CI rows from the ci-guarantees report, so 10 of 10.

metrics.label: Days of the last 7 with report rows for both repos
Hours since the newest store box copy
Failed steps in the last daily run
Tracked metrics the report page shows: 8 ranked, tests (full suite set), CI

onMiss: Every missed metric gets a fix step under p5 with duty <dutyId>/<metricKey> and a live job that lands a code change for it, started with rlm.create_session; when the step already has a live job, steer it with scripts/job-steer.ts. Read the flagged items first: they name the missing days, the ranked rows the page misses, the newest backup and each failed step with its error. The run is code-health.timer on us-metal02 (systemctl --user status code-health.timer code-health.service, log ~/.local/state/virev/code-health.log), the code is auto-sns-agent scripts/dev/code-health-daily.mjs and apps/llm-wiki/scripts/code-health.py, and the page is served by llm-wiki.service from the checkout. report_days_7d: find why the run left that day or repo out and fix it; the next run backfills missed days of the last week by itself. backup_age_h: fix the backup step (ssh and scp to root@100.84.91.26, backups/code-health). source_errors: fix each failed step's cause. ranked_metrics_shown: each ranked_missing item names the metric, the repo and the page row that is missing or behind the store, the junit suite the day's test load lacks, or the day's missing ci-guarantees rows. A missing suite means load-tests found no junit-log block for it in the dev/sieun verify-dev push runs of the last day: find whether that job did not run, ran without scripts/ci/junit-log.sh, or printed a block load-tests skipped (its stderr names a corrupt block), fix it, and rerun the day; a suite stays expected until scripts/ci/junit-suites.mjs drops its task, so when CI dropped the task for good, drop it from that table in the same change. Missing ci-guarantees rows mean load-ci found no fresh report in the ci-cd-health.yml job logs: fix the guarantees step or load-ci and rerun the day. For the page rows, when they lag the store, find why the page step (code-health.py table, which calls render in code_health_page.py) did not write that row, and when the store has no number, find why code-health.py or code_health_new.py left that metric out of the run. Treat a failed load-tests or load-ci step as real even when the precheck lists it as excused, because tests and CI now come from the CI job logs; plan step p14 removes the excuse from the precheck. After the fix lands, rerun the day with systemctl --user start code-health.service on us-metal02, then rerun the precheck and report each metric before and after. A metric at 999999 means the precheck could not read its input: fix that first, in scripts/duties/code-health-report.ts in sieun-pi legacy/prime/user-history. Nothing goes to an outside party.
